description: An ambitious junior Computer Science major with a heavy background in cybersecurity and competitive hacking who prefers hands-on implementation over theoretical modeling.

nodes.title: OS Services and Dual-Mode Operation
nodes.description: Core review of operating system services, system calls, and the dual-mode operation of the CPU (kernel vs. user mode).
nodes.personalizationRationale: The student's strong_prior_exposure allows for a high-level conceptual review of foundational structures without remedial scaffolding.

nodes.title: Architectural Design and Performance Analysis
nodes.description: In-depth analysis of monolithic, layered, and microkernel architectures, focusing on performance tradeoffs and context-switching overhead.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Given the student's strong_prior_exposure, this node explores system architecture from a performance and design-tradeoff perspective.

nodes.description: Detailed exploration of process states, the Process Control Block (PCB), and the mechanics of context switching.
nodes.title: Process Life Cycle and Management
nodes.personalizationRationale: Core process management is essential for all students, but is framed here for those with strong_prior_exposure to C-based execution.

nodes.description: Comparative analysis of Inter-Process Communication (IPC) via shared memory versus message passing, focusing on cache coherency and scalability.
nodes.title: Advanced IPC and Synchronization Overheads
nodes.personalizationRationale: Strong_prior_exposure enables the student to investigate complex IPC bottlenecks and synchronization overhead at a systems level.
Standard threading libraries are required core content, though the student's strong_prior_exposure will facilitate faster implementation.
nodes.description: Survey of threading models (Many-to-One, One-to-One, Many-to-Many) and the POSIX Pthreads library.
nodes.title: Threading Models and Libraries

nodes.personalizationRationale: Scheduling theory is a mandatory core component that builds directly on the student's existing understanding of process execution.
nodes.description: Examination of CPU scheduling criteria and advanced algorithms such as Multi-Level Feedback Queues and Linux CFS.
nodes.title: CPU Scheduling Algorithms and Criteria

nodes.description: Comprehensive assessment of material from Chapters 1-5, focusing on system structures, processes, and scheduling.
nodes.title: Midterm Assessment Review (Ch. 1-5)
nodes.personalizationRationale: A required midterm assessment checkpoint to ensure mastery of foundational concepts regardless of strong_prior_exposure.
Strong_prior_exposure allows for a direct application of mutexes to solve classic concurrency problems in required OS modules.
nodes.title: Synchronization Primitives: Mutexes and Semaphores
nodes.description: Introduction to the critical-section problem and synchronization primitives including Mutex locks and Semaphores.

nodes.personalizationRationale: For a student with strong_prior_exposure, this node moves beyond basic locks into hardware-accelerated synchronization techniques.
nodes.title: Hardware Atomics and Lock-Free Programming
nodes.description: Exploration of lock-free data structures and hardware-level atomic operations like Test-And-Set and Compare-And-Swap.

nodes.personalizationRationale: Deadlock characterization is a mandatory core topic that ensures all students can model system safety analytically.
nodes.title: Deadlock Characterization and Avoidance
nodes.description: Study of the four necessary conditions for deadlock and the Banker's Algorithm for deadlock avoidance.

nodes.personalizationRationale: Strong_prior_exposure helps the student grasp address translation quickly, allowing focus on the hardware/software interface.
nodes.description: Core mechanics of contiguous memory allocation, fragmentation, and the transition to paging with page tables.
nodes.title: Main Memory and Paging Structures

nodes.personalizationRationale: This required core content is vital for the memory management programming projects which the student will undertake.
nodes.title: Virtual Memory and Page Replacement
nodes.description: Detailed study of demand paging and page replacement algorithms like LRU, FIFO, and Optimal.

nodes.personalizationRationale: Strong_prior_exposure suggests the student is ready to evaluate memory management performance in large-scale production environments.
nodes.title: Advanced Memory Performance and Thrashing Analysis
nodes.description: Analysis of TLB (Translation Lookaside Buffer) reach, hugepage support, and the performance impact of thrashing in modern kernels.
Survey of I/O hardware, polling vs. interrupts, and DMA (Direct Memory Access) mechanisms.
nodes.title: I/O Systems and Hardware Interfaces
nodes.personalizationRationale: Understanding I/O interfaces is a core requirement for completing the cumulative syllabus for the final exam.
Every student must master file system implementation as it forms a major part of the cumulative final assessment.
nodes.description: Investigation of file system implementation strategies including allocation methods (contiguous, linked, indexed) and directory structures.
nodes.title: File System Implementation and Allocation

nodes.description: Cumulative review of the entire syllabus from OS structures through file systems in preparation for the final exam.
nodes.title: Cumulative Final Review and Exam Prep
nodes.personalizationRationale: A mandatory final assessment node for this required course, regardless of the student's strong_prior_exposure tier.
